rationale: Base config: trainer defaults tuned in the single-algorithm cards.
Lower learning rate: slower but steadier Q-value fitting.
Higher learning rate: faster progress, risk of unstable bootstrapped targets.
Shorter horizon (~20 decisions): favours immediate pickups over planning.
Fast epsilon decay: exploit early, risk locking in a poor route habit.
Slow epsilon decay: explore for 60% of the budget.
Small replay buffer: fresher, more on-policy data, less diversity.
Small minibatch: noisier gradients, same number of updates.
Late learning start: a more diverse buffer before the first update.
Hard target copy every 1k gradient steps (hard_update_interval) instead of soft Polyak updates.
